uncertainties: Interpreted the specification's 'ordinary authorization' blocker rule to exempt requests with exact jurisdiction domain='resolution' and operation='resolve'; because reference kind is explicitly opaque and blockers have no immutable-reference linkage field, no additional semantic linkage between the resolution target and a blocker can be proven by this interface.

Interpreted supporting_artifacts[*].ref_id as required to resolve to a request references[*].ref_id because supporting artifacts are described as separate references, although the JSON Schema cannot express that cross-field relation.

The dict-based evaluate interface cannot detect duplicate raw JSON member names after decoding; the implementation detects cycles, non-string keys, non-finite numbers, host-only values, and UTF-8 encoding failures that remain observable in decoded Python values.

Applied the AuthorityState canonical-JSON procedure to immutable-reference identity, request_sha256, and receipt semantic identity because those fields require deterministic SHA-256 identities but their sections do not restate a separate canonicalization algorithm.

For structurally malformed requests whose exact list values cannot be represented by the receipt schema or canonicalized safely, the receipt preserves only schema-valid request list fields and otherwise emits empty arrays; fully valid requests preserve exact copies.

Did not impose uniqueness on request ref_id values, supporting-artifact ids, conflict ids, or residue ids because neither the specification nor schema states those uniqueness constraints; duplicate local ref_id values therefore remain structurally accepted.

Treated timestamp strings matching the schema pattern as malformed if they are not calendar-valid UTC timestamps; leap-second ':60' values are rejected, while arbitrary fractional-second precision is compared exactly.
deviations: The available GitHub write interface commits one file per contents-API write. authority_e.py was committed first at f0b5459e9a2a8551d0f625e21a96313d87127ec2, then test_authority_e.py at 75e22edf20c531fb50ed47cb1d199dfa15a5a6b8; the latter commit, where both exact file states coexist, is treated as the immutable implementation/test freeze.

The three aperture Git blob identities were independently verified through exact path/ref retrieval before their contents were consumed. A post-freeze attempt to re-retrieve the same three authorized raw paths solely to recompute their launch-supplied SHA-256 values was blocked by the web fetch environment, so the aperture SHA-256 fields record the exact launch-supplied expected values rather than an independently recomputed digest. No unrelated content was returned.
